_README: Discovery + auto-tick settings for session-restore.
Nothing here names a repository. A background scan reads ~/.claude/projects/,
resolves each conversation's real working directory from its transcript, and
records it in sessions-registry.json as a PROJECT holding its CONVERSATIONS.
WHICH of them reopen is your choice -- make it with select-sessions.ps1 (or
ccs), not here. These numbers only decide what arrives PRE-TICKED.
recencyDays           a newly discovered PROJECT arrives ticked if it was
worked in within this many days.
sessionWindowDays     within a project, a newly discovered CONVERSATION
arrives ticked if it was active within this many days.
autoTickPerDirectory  how many conversations per project the roll keeps
ticked, newest first. RECOMPUTED ON EVERY SCAN, so the
set follows the work: return to an old slice and it
re-ticks itself, move on and it falls out. Without a
ceiling a repo with sixteen live conversations would
open sixteen tabs.
Conversations you TOUCH in the picker are PINNED and
the roll never changes them -- otherwise the scan would
undo your choices within the hour. A pinned+ticked one
spends part of this ceiling, so the total stays bounded
however it was set. Press U in the picker to hand one
back to the roll.
registryWindowDays    conversations older than this are not tracked at all.
Bounds the scan: without it every historical transcript
on the machine would be read on every pass.
maxSessions           cap on tabs opened in ONE restore. The tool SAYS how
many it dropped -- it never truncates silently. Use
-All to ignore it once.
excludePatterns       PowerShell -like patterns matched against the resolved
working directory; environment variables are expanded.
The home directory is always excluded, pattern or not.
DO NOT exclude '*\.claude\worktrees\*'. It was there
briefly, on the reasoning that two sessions in one tree
share a git index -- which is backwards. A git worktree
has its OWN index; 'one worktree per lane' is the
MITIGATION for that hazard, not the hazard. Excluding
them hid a live session working in .claude/worktrees/D1
and no amount of rescanning could surface it.
A stale worktree is handled by sessionWindowDays on its
own: measured, the preserved bounded-contexts worktree
lists 22 conversations and ticks ZERO, because all of
them are older than the window. Listed, restores
nothing. Fold it away with LEFT in the picker, or untick
the project.
NONE of these gate the restore. Once a conversation is ticked, your tick wins
and it reopens; staleness is reported, never acted on. One source of truth.
Everything for this tool lives in this folder. Your selections are in
sessions-registry.json beside this file (gitignored -- the paths are local).
select-sessions.ps1            choose what reopens
restore-sessions.ps1 -DryRun   see exactly what would come back
restore-sessions.ps1 -Scan     refresh the registry now (the hourly task)
